items.title: When Are Images Needed in Multimodal Machine Translation? Text-Only Routing for On-Demand Visual Context
items.summary_1line: Proposes PreVIR, a lightweight text-only router that decides from the source sentence alone whether to invoke visual features in English-to-Chinese machine translation, reducing visual calls while keeping quality near always-on multimodal inference.

items.title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier
items.summary_1line: Search-RSI is a self-improvement framework for multimodal search agents that expands the retrieval world with new tasks and evidence, reporting 9.8 and 9.5 point average accuracy gains at 9B and 27B across nine benchmarks.
items.editor_note: Self-improving multimodal search agent; reports 9.8 and 9.5 point gains at 9B and 27B.

items.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
items.summary_1line: Describes a two-tier industrial framework for automated UX attribution in web search: a fine-tuned Gemini XS telemetry model for macro sentiment regression detection, and a Gemini 3.0 Pro multimodal model for layout-level diagnostics.
items.editor_note: Production setup at Google search: Gemini models for UX regression detection and layout diagnostics.

items.title: KernelShift: Benchmarking Kernel Optimization Across Evolving Hardware
items.summary_1line: KernelShift is a benchmark that tests coding agents on CPU kernel optimization across Arm Neon, SVE, SVE2 and SME2, finding agents beat the compiler and some libraries but lag KleidiAI and struggle with SME2.
items.editor_note: Off-theme: coding agents beat the compiler on Arm kernels but lag KleidiAI and struggle with SME2.

items.title: Test-Time Latent Computation to Improve Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Proposes Lobals, a training-free decoding method that re-runs a contiguous window of MLLM layers with the strongest visual-token attention to revisit visual evidence, reporting gains on vision-language, hallucination, and vision-centric tasks.
items.editor_note: Training-free decoding that re-runs the most vision-attentive layers to revisit visual evidence.

items.title: Parsing Visual Latents for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning
items.summary_1line: LatentParse is a training-free framework that uses an analyst VLM to parse CLIP, DINOv3 and VGGT features into a text report of spatial evidence, improving five VLMs by 0.7-2.4 points on three spatial benchmarks.
items.editor_note: Training-free parsing of CLIP, DINOv3 and VGGT features into text; 0.7 to 2.4 point spatial gains.

items.title: What People Choose Not to Say: A Multimodal Benchmark for Fine-Grained Information Manipulation in Conversations
items.summary_1line: Introduces InfoCon, a multimodal benchmark that labels six fine-grained information manipulation strategies in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, and fabrication, plus a coarse consistency label, and benchmarks representative multimodal models on it.
items.editor_note: Benchmark for detecting withholding, leakage and fabrication in multimodal conversations.

items.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
items.summary_1line: Introduces ToolSmith, a framework that automatically generates and reuses new tools on top of a lean base library for multimodal search agents, evaluated on 13 benchmarks with gains that grow with backbone size.
items.editor_note: Search agents generate and reuse their own tools; gains grow with backbone size across 13 benchmarks.

items.title: EVA: Evidence-seeking Visual Agent for Hallucination-Resistant Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary_1line: Proposes EVA, a visual agent that reduces multimodal LLM hallucinations by gathering external visual evidence through iterative tool replanning, verifying answers against that evidence, and invoking tools selectively.
items.editor_note: Agent verifies answers against tool-gathered visual evidence and calls tools selectively.

items.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
items.summary_1line: An empirical study finding that adding a generated helper image to visual question answering lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 points across 13 model pairs, with declines on nine of ten tasks.
items.editor_note: Negative result: generated helper images lowered accuracy on nine of ten tasks.

editorial.tldr: This is a research-theme thread, not one event: 22 items, mostly arXiv preprints, from Nov 9 to Nov 25 on visual agents, multimodal benchmarks and hallucination fixes. Mid-month the work shifted from new benchmarks (WebArena-Pro, MM-ReportBench, Google's Multimodal Knowledge Agent Benchmark) to agents that fetch visual evidence with tools.
editorial.whats_new: A Nov 25 study found that adding a generated helper image to visual QA lowered mean accuracy by 3.7 points across 13 model pairs, while EVA the same day cut hallucinations by checking answers against tool-gathered visual evidence.
editorial.why_it_matters: For multimodal agents, the reliable gains in this thread come from grounding answers in fetched or re-read visual evidence; generating extra images or always sending pixels adds cost without a proven accuracy gain.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before adding image generation or always-on image inputs to a multimodal agent, run an ablation on your own eval set; prefer zoom, crop and re-check tools that tie each answer to visual evidence.

status.detail: Preprints only, no shipped products: evidence-seeking visual agents are the common direction, and one negative result questions image generation as a reasoning aid.

Agents zoom, search and build tools to gather visual evidence
beats.summary: Instead of reasoning over one image in context, these agents call tools to crop, search or remember visual state.

beats.headline: Training and decoding fixes target visually ungrounded answers
Industry papers use vision where it pays: cover photos, UX diagnostics, on-demand routing
Evidence-checking helps; generated helper images hurt

open_questions: Does any lab ship a production visual agent that verifies answers against tool-gathered evidence, as EVA does?
Does the 3.7-point accuracy drop from generated helper images hold for frontier models outside the 13 tested pairs?
Will WebArena-Pro or Google's Multimodal Knowledge Agent Benchmark get adopted as a standard leaderboard?
Do text-only routers like PreVIR cut visual-token cost in agent workloads, not only in translation?
